sections.h2: Where do I record a deed in Macon County, NC?
sections.html:
A deed for Macon County land is recorded with the county Register of Deeds in Franklin. Macon County government works from 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734, and the county switchboard at (828) 349-2000 can connect you to the Register of Deeds.

The county directory lists a vault line and several extensions for the office. Ask the office for its recording hours and its same-day cutoff before you plan a closing around it.

The Register of Deeds is elected by county voters for a two-year term under G.S. 161-1. The office applies the same statewide recording rules used in all North Carolina counties, so a Macon County deed follows the same format, fee and tax rules as a deed filed elsewhere.

sections.h2: What do recording fees and the excise tax cost in Macon County?
sections.html:
Fees come from G.S. 161-10, and the excise tax comes from G.S. 105-228.30. The register collects both before a deed is recorded.

  • General instruments: $26.00 covers the first 15 pages, then $4.00 per added page.
  • Mortgages and deeds of trust: $64.00 covers the first 35 pages, then $4.00 per added page.
  • Satisfactions and cancellations of mortgages and deeds of trust: no fee.
  • Extra instruments in one document: $10.00 each.
  • Excise tax on a deed: $1.00 for each $500.00 of value, with any fractional part counted as a full $500.00.

The seller is the transferor and owes the excise tax. The register sends half to the county general fund and passes the other half, less refunds and the county's allowance, to the Department of Revenue each month. Closing attorneys in Franklin normally deduct the tax from the seller's proceeds and deliver it with the deed.

sections.h2: Why does the order of recording matter for a Macon County seller?
sections.html:
Recording sets priority. G.S. 47-18 provides that deeds, contracts to convey, options and leases of more than three years do not bind lien creditors or purchasers for value until they are registered in the county where the land sits, and the earlier registration wins.

A parcel that has passed through several families can carry old rights of way or boundary agreements. Have the closing attorney search the Macon County index for each prior owner, and ask the Land Records office for the parcel map so the legal description on the new deed matches the tax parcel.

A recorded deed does not by itself settle the tax bill. The county assesses property as of January 1, so ask the tax office who is billed for the current year and plan the proration with your closing attorney.

sections.h2: What does the Macon County Land Records office do?
sections.html:
The Land Records office, also called the Mapping Office, is on the main level of the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in downtown Franklin. It is the place to get property cards, parcel maps and county maps, and it has public terminals for document searches, property searches, collection information and assessment data.

The tax office also links an address change form, property tax forms and a land records search from its page, so many owners can pull a map or a parcel record before they visit. A seller preparing a listing can print the parcel map to check the lot lines against the deed.

The Tax Department itself sits in the annex at 5 West Main Street. It posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the county scroll.

sections.h2: Which Macon County dates matter after I record a deed?
sections.html:
The county tax calendar drives most of what follows a sale. The Macon County Tax Department lists these dates on its home page.

Important dates listed by the Macon County Tax Department
DateWhat happens
January 1Date of assessment; personal property ownership and place of taxation are set as of this date
January 1 to 31Listing period for personal property, except tagged motor vehicles, and for exemption and exclusion filing
January 5Last day to pay property taxes without interest
January 6Interest begins
AprilBoard of Equalization and Review meets
April 15Last date to file listings with a prior approved extension
AugustCurrent-year tax bills processed and mailed

The 2026 board began meeting April 7, 2026 and adjourned April 17, 2026, and appeals had to be received or postmarked by that day. The tax office also notes a 2027 reappraisal and offers an online appeal portal, so check there after any new values are mailed.

sections.h2: What is Macon County like for home sellers?
sections.html:
Macon County is a county whose communities include Franklin, Highlands and Nantahala. The Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 population at 39,232, up 6.0 percent from the April 2020 base, and counts 515.58 square miles of land.

  • Persons 65 and over: 31.7 percent.
  • Housing units: 27,700, against 18,406 households for 2020 to 2024.
  • Persons per household: 2.04.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 77.6 percent.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $251,900.
  • Median gross rent: $803, and median household income: $59,061 in 2024 dollars.
  • Accommodation and food services sales: $205,516 thousand in 2022.

Those figures show more housing units than households. A buyer who plans a second home or a rental will want to see the recorded deed and any restrictions on file with the register.

sections.h2: What if the Macon County owner has died?
sections.html:
Start with the clerk of superior court, not the register of deeds. The directory lists the Estates and Special Proceedings line at (828) 349-7204, and that office can explain whether a small estate affidavit fits or whether the estate needs a personal representative.

For intestate estates, G.S. 28A-25-1 permits an affidavit filed with the clerk in the county of domicile when personal property less liens does not exceed $20,000, any time after 30 days from death. A surviving spouse who is the only heir may reach a limit up to $30,000 after the spousal allowance. The affidavit describes each tract of real property the decedent owned.

Once authority is in place, the signed deed goes to the Register of Deeds for recording. Bring the certified death record if the register or the title company asks for it.

faqs.q: Where is the Macon County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is part of Macon County government in Franklin, whose main address is 5 West Main Street, Franklin, NC 28734. Call (828) 349-2000 and ask for the Register of Deeds to confirm hours.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Macon County?
faqs.a: A general instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages and $4.00 for each added page, and the excise tax is $1.00 per $500.00 of value. The Macon County register collects both before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does Macon County have a separate tax scroll for Highlands?
faqs.a: Yes, the Macon County Tax Department posts a separate tax scroll for Highlands next to the main county scroll. Ask the tax office which scroll applies to your parcel.

faqs.q: When do Macon County property taxes become late?
faqs.a: Interest begins January 6, and January 5 is the last day to pay without interest. The county mails current-year bills in August.

faqs.q: Where can I get a parcel map in Macon County?
faqs.a: Visit the Land Records office in the Macon County Courthouse on the Square in Franklin, or use the land records search linked from the tax office page. Property cards, parcel maps and county maps are available there.
